texto:
AI referral traffic is the stream of human visits a website receives when someone clicks a link inside an answer produced by a generative artificial intelligence (AI) assistant, such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Perplexity or Microsoft Copilot. It exists as a category because those assistants now sit between a question and the open web, much as search engines did, and site owners want to know how many people the assistants actually send onwards. The term describes the click, not the mention: a brand that is named in an answer but never clicked generates no AI referral traffic at all.
In most markets the stream is small. Ahrefs data across 76,000 websites, published in February 2026, put ChatGPT at about 0.21% of traffic against nearly 40% for Google. Its growth rate, its apparent value per visit and the difficulty of counting it accurately are what keep it on marketing agendas. Being cited is a separate matter, measured as AI visibility, and the work of influencing those answers is known as GEO, or generative engine optimization.
How a visit gets labelled
Analytics software decides where a visit came from using two signals. The first is the HTTP referrer, a header the browser sends when a user follows a link, naming the page the user left. A click from chatgpt.com in a web browser normally carries chatgpt.com as its referring domain, or at least its origin under the default referrer policies modern browsers apply. The second is campaign tagging: Urchin Tracking Module (UTM) parameters, such as utm_source, appended to the destination link.
The sequence runs as follows. A user asks a question. The assistant retrieves pages, writes an answer and attaches citations or link cards. The user clicks one. The destination site's tag, whether Google Analytics 4 (GA4), Adobe Analytics or Microsoft Clarity, records a session and reads the referrer and any UTM values. A rule set then assigns the session to a channel.
That last step is where AI referral traffic became a formal category. Google's August 2025 guidance told GA4 users to build a custom channel group with a channel called "AI Chatbots", defined by a regular expression matching fragments such as "openai", "chatgpt", "gemini", "copilot" and "perplexity". Because channels are evaluated in order and the pattern also matched the bare string "ai", the rule could sweep in unrelated referrers. Standard properties are limited to two custom channel groups, each with up to 50 channels.
On May 13, 2026, Google made the step automatic. GA4 added an AI Assistant channel to its Default Channel Group, assigning the medium "ai-assistant" and the campaign label "(ai-assistant)" when it recognises an AI assistant referrer. Google has not published the full list of recognised assistants. Microsoft Clarity had already split out AI Platform and Paid AI Platform channel groups on August 29, 2025, the second covering sessions that start from advertisements inside AI experiences.
Referrers fail more often than they work in some contexts. Clicks from native mobile and desktop apps frequently arrive with no referrer and are classed as direct traffic. A link marked "noreferrer" strips the header entirely. When Google's AI Mode launched in the US in May 2025, its links did exactly that, and clicks showed up as direct or unknown until Google called it a bug on May 23, 2025. John Mueller of Google Search Relations described the behaviour as "unexpected". UTM tags exist partly to repair this. OpenAI began adding UTM parameters to links in ChatGPT's "More" section in June 2025; before that only citation links carried them, and the rest were logged as direct.
Origin and evolution
AI referral traffic did not exist as a measurable stream until assistants began linking out. Perplexity, launched in December 2022, cited sources from the start. Microsoft's Bing Chat, introduced in February 2023, attached footnoted links to its answers. ChatGPT gained live web results through browsing features in 2023 and a dedicated search product on October 31, 2024. Google's AI Overviews, rolled out in the US in May 2024, and AI Mode, in May 2025, complicate the picture: their clicks arrive from google.com and are usually counted as organic search, not as AI referrals.
The volumes rose quickly from a tiny base. Similarweb reported that ChatGPT referrals to news sites grew from under 1 million visits between January and May 2024 to more than 25 million in the same months of 2025. Adobe Analytics, drawing on more than 1 trillion visits to US retail sites, found traffic from generative AI tools rose 693.4% year on year over the November and December 2025 holiday season, according to Adobe's January 7, 2026 release. Adobe noted that the base of users "remains modest", which is what makes triple-digit growth arithmetically easy.
Volumes can also fall abruptly when a platform changes how it cites. Josh Blyskal of Profound, analysing more than one billion ChatGPT citations, reported that ChatGPT referral traffic fell 52% from July 21, 2025 as citations concentrated on Reddit and Wikipedia. After ChatGPT 5.3 launched on March 3, 2026, Olivier de Segonzac of Resoneo measured average unique domains per response falling from about 19.8 to about 15.9.
Why it matters for marketers
The case for attention rests on quality rather than quantity. On its own site, Ahrefs found AI search visitors made up 0.5% of visits but 12.1% of sign-ups, which it expressed as conversion at about 23 times the rate of organic search. Microsoft Clarity, across 1,277 publisher and news domains, measured sign-up conversion of 1.66% for AI traffic against 0.15% for search, with AI referrals still under 1% of visits but up 155.6% over eight months while search grew 24.0%.
For publishers, the stream matters because it is one of the few things they receive in exchange for content that AI companies crawl. The gap between pages fetched and visitors returned is tracked as the crawl-to-referral ratio. On August 13, 2026, Microsoft Clarity added a card that divides crawler requests by referral sessions per AI operator; its sample screenshot showed 6,000 requests per referral, though Microsoft did not present that as a benchmark. Decisions about blocking crawlers also turn on it. Hangcheng Zhao of Rutgers and Ron Berman of Wharton found that news publishers which blocked large language model crawlers lost roughly 7% of weekly traffic within six weeks, but traced the loss mainly to direct visits, not to missing referral clicks.
Limitations and disputes
The share figures disagree because they measure different things. Ahrefs' 0.21% covers ChatGPT across 76,000 sites. Maximilian Kaiser and Christian Schulze put ChatGPT at under 0.2% of sessions on 973 e-commerce sites. Semrush found AI assistants and Google AI Mode together sent 0.48% of sessions to US manufacturing and industrial sites between January and July 2026. Datos, a Semrush company, reported AI tools at 1.65% of US desktop events in the first quarter of 2026, but that figure counts visits to AI tools themselves, not visits they send elsewhere, and excludes mobile.
The conversion claims are contested directly. Kaiser and Schulze, covering August 2024 to July 2025 and more than 50,000 ChatGPT-referred transactions, found ChatGPT referrals converted worse than every channel except paid social, with organic search about 13% better. Their work was later published in Marketing Science. The higher multiples come mostly from single-company or vendor datasets with small denominators; Ryan Law of Ahrefs said of early click-through rates that they were "probably the highest they'll ever be as the novelty of this format wears off".
Undercounting is the third dispute. Similarweb's panel study of US desktop users, covering July to December 2025, found that among visits influenced by an AI recommendation, only 8.8% came through a direct AI referral, while 55.9% arrived via search, typically a branded query typed later. Referral data therefore captures only the visible edge of AI influence. App traffic logged as direct, Google AI features logged as organic, and inconsistent assistant lists across analytics vendors push in the same direction. No industry body audits the classification.
Not the same as
- AI crawler or bot traffic: automated requests from systems such as GPTBot or ClaudeBot fetching pages. These are machines, usually excluded from analytics, and they are the numerator in the crawl-to-referral ratio, not part of referral traffic.
- AI visibility: how often an assistant names or cites a brand. It measures exposure inside the answer; AI referral traffic measures the clicks that follow.
- Traffic from AI Overviews and AI Mode: clicks from Google's AI features normally carry a google.com referrer and land in organic search reports. Some vendors, Semrush among them, count AI Mode separately.
- Agentic traffic: visits made by AI agents browsing or transacting on a user's behalf. The visitor is software acting for a human, which analytics tools may record as a bot, a human session, or both.
Recent developments
Measurement tooling has moved faster than the traffic itself. GA4's AI Assistant channel, live since May 13, 2026, replaced hand-built regular expressions for many sites. Similarweb data published on June 11, 2026 showed ChatGPT's share of generative AI website traffic falling to 52.7% as Gemini reached 27.3% and Claude 8.9%, a shift that changes which referrers matter. Microsoft Clarity's AI tooling, including its Citations dashboard, generally available since May 13, 2026, and a September 29, 2026 update letting brands edit what counts as a branded AI query, pairs exposure data with referral data in one product. As of October 2026, no shared standard defines which referrers count as AI assistants, and the main figures still come from vendors with products to sell in the category.
Timeline
- December 2022: Perplexity launches with cited sources in its answers.
- February 7, 2023: Microsoft introduces Bing Chat with footnoted links.
- May 2024: Google rolls out AI Overviews in the US.
- August 2024: Start of the Kaiser and Schulze study window, the first year of ChatGPT linking out to e-commerce sites.
- October 31, 2024: OpenAI launches ChatGPT search.
- May 20, 2025: Google launches AI Mode in the US.
- May 23, 2025: Google confirms AI Mode links stripping referrers is a bug.
- June 13, 2025: ChatGPT starts adding UTM parameters to "More" links.
- June 16, 2025: Ahrefs publishes its 23x conversion analysis.
- July 2, 2025: Similarweb reports ChatGPT referrals to news sites topped 25 million in January to May.
- July 21, 2025: Profound data shows ChatGPT referral traffic beginning a 52% fall.
- August 2025: Google publishes AI Chatbots custom channel group guidance.
- August 29, 2025: Microsoft Clarity adds AI Platform and Paid AI Platform channel groups.
- October 24, 2025: Kaiser and Schulze e-commerce findings reported.
- November 6, 2025: Microsoft Clarity publishes AI traffic conversion data for 1,277 domains.
- January 7, 2026: Adobe reports a 693.4% rise in generative AI traffic to US retail sites over the 2025 holidays.
- February 11, 2026: Ahrefs publishes ChatGPT versus Google traffic comparison.
- March 3, 2026: ChatGPT 5.3 launches; later analysis finds fewer unique domains per answer.
- April 21, 2026: Zhao and Berman revise their crawler-blocking paper.
- May 13, 2026: GA4 adds the AI Assistant default channel.
- June 21, 2026: Similarweb publishes "The Downstream Impact of AI Visibility".
- August 13, 2026: Microsoft Clarity adds the AI Scrape-to-Referral Ratio card.
- September 8, 2026: Semrush publishes manufacturing study putting AI at 0.48% of sessions.
- September 29, 2026: Microsoft Clarity lets brands edit branded AI query terms.

Summary
Who: Website owners, publishers and retailers receive AI referral traffic; OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Perplexity and Microsoft operate the assistants that send it; Google Analytics, Adobe Analytics and Microsoft Clarity classify it; Ahrefs, Similarweb, Semrush, Datos and academic researchers measure it.
What: Human website visits that follow a click on a link inside a generative AI assistant's answer, identified by the referrer header or UTM tags and grouped into dedicated analytics channels.
When: The stream emerged with cited AI answers from Perplexity in December 2022 and Bing Chat in February 2023, grew after ChatGPT search launched on October 31, 2024, and gained a default GA4 channel on May 13, 2026.
Where: In analytics reports on any website, most visibly in GA4's AI Assistant channel and Clarity's AI Platform groups; much AI-driven traffic instead lands in direct or organic search.
Why: It is the measurable return publishers and brands get from AI systems that use their content. Its small share, disputed conversion value and systematic undercounting make it a contested input to budget, content and crawler-blocking decisions.
